definitions.explanation: A formal written expression of gratitude, typically sent after receiving a gift, attending an event, or being helped. An important part of Japanese social etiquette.

examples.japanese: お{中元|ちゅうげん}の{礼状|れいじょう}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a thank-you letter for the mid-year gift.

examples.japanese: {面接|めんせつ}の{後|あと}、{礼状|れいじょう}を{送|おく}るのがマナーだ。
examples.english: It is good manners to send a thank-you letter after an interview.

examples.japanese: {贈|おく}り{物|もの}が{届|とど}いたら、できるだけ{早|はや}く{礼状|れいじょう}を{出|だ}すようにしている。
examples.english: When I receive a gift, I try to send a thank-you letter as soon as possible.

notes:
USAGE: Sending a {礼状|れいじょう} is an important part of Japanese social customs. Common occasions include receiving seasonal gifts (お{中元|ちゅうげん}, お{歳暮|せいぼ}), attending weddings, after job interviews, and after receiving hospitality.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {礼状|れいじょう}を{書|か}く: to write a thank-you letter
- {礼状|れいじょう}を{送|おく}る / {出|だ}す: to send a thank-you letter
- お{礼|れい}の{手紙|てがみ}: thank-you letter (more casual phrasing)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {礼状|れいじょう}: formal thank-you letter
- {挨拶状|あいさつじょう}: greeting card/letter (broader, includes seasonal greetings)
- {年賀状|ねんがじょう}: New Year's card (specific type of seasonal letter)
